risks: only 3 validation windows: weight estimation is high variance
diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~18% of its level). Seasonality is strong (period 52): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. Predictability is middling — structured signal and irregular noise are balanced. The series reads as ambiguous by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (8 points, ~0% of the sample). Across validation windows the model ranking is moderate (Kendall tau 0.415), which favours a weighted combination.

We have tested weighted, median pool1, dba pool1, mean pool5? not yet. We have not tested mean pool5. Let's try mean pool5.

deterministic baseline: median, robust to outlying models

deterministic baseline: mean over the 5 models with the most consistent ranking across windows

deterministic baseline: mean over the 7 models with the most consistent ranking across windows
deterministic baseline: trimmed_mean over the 7 models with the most consistent ranking across windows
deterministic baseline: mean over the 9 models with the most consistent ranking across windows
deterministic baseline: trimmed_mean over the 9 models with the most consistent ranking across windows
deterministic baseline: weights from a gradient-boosted model trained across every other series in this run (leave-one-series-out)
Test a weighted combination using inverse_error on the moderately stable pool2 to see if it improves over the baseline weighted w1.
Test a weighted combination on the most stable pool (pool1) using inverse_error weights to see if a focused weighted approach improves over the baseline mean.
Test the best single model hypothesis – use catboost alone as it tops the error table.
Test a simple median combination over pool1 to see if a robust median improves over mean.
Test a simple mean over pool4 to see if a smaller, more stable pool improves over the current leader.
Test a robust median over pool2 to see if a different subset improves performance.
Test a trimmed‑mean over the stable pool4 to see if trimming outliers improves the weighted average.
Test a deterministic Bayesian averaging (dba) on the stable pool4 to see if it outperforms the weighted inverse_error approach.
Test a weighted inverse_error combination on pool3 to see if a different subset improves over the current leader.
Test a median combination on pool2 to see if a robust non‑weighted average improves over the current leader.
test a deterministic Bayesian averaging on the stable pool1 to see if it beats weighted inverse_error.
Test a simple mean over the stable pool5 to see if a smaller, more stable pool improves over the current leader.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean' (a seeded deterministic baseline) as the best of 22 backtested attempts, score 1.0. Series context: trend strength 0.7774 and seasonal strength 0.7819; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.415); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 3.289.
